22.text: place. The craving of the natives for it is aptly expressed in a tale well

23.text: known to all tribes of northeastern Siberia.

24.text: In the time of a tobacco famine, when all the people were nearly mad

25.text: because they had nothing to smoke, one well-to-do reindeer-breeder possessed

26.text: a large pouch quite filled with tobacco, but would not share it with any one.

27.text: At last his own brother asked for a pipeful, and was refused. The next day

28.text: he overtook the owner of the tobacco on the tundra, stabbed him from behind

29.text: with his spear, ripped open his breast, and took out his lungs, which he found

30.text: covered with soot. He scraped away a part of this, and used it to fill his

31.text: pipe. The pouch he left untouched. When caught by the Cossacks and

32.text: brought before the Russian magistrate, he showed him the big pouch and the

33.text: sooty lungs, and was acquitted of the charge.

34.text: Tobacco has found its way from Siberia far eastward into arctic America.

37.text: “Farther on live men who dissever themselves at will. They stay among

38.text: the trees on the shores of the lakes, cleft in halves; but, at the slightest

39.text: rustling, the parts come together, and they dive into the water. These, too,

40.text: have a longing for tobacco, and pay for it with large fish and otters.

41.text: “Still deeper in the woods live dwarfs not larger than the fore-arm of a

42.text: man. Three of them can hardly overcome one goose. They dwell in trees,

43.text: and buy tobacco with the skins of the lynx and of the muskrat.
